unwalkedPanels.why: The home screen, and it is COVERED SOMEWHERE ELSE rather than uncovered: round-11.1/v1 "Constellation" is a WebGL canvas composition, so a computed-style walk can read nothing painted on it. tests/home.js measures it FROM THE PIXELS instead — 16 elements, worst 4.23:1, on the rendered frame — which check 14 already names. Two DOM checkers over one canvas would be one checker rotting.

The voice panel mid-listen. Reaching it needs a live audio device: main.js hides the talk button entirely when voice_readiness refuses, and the panel only paints once start_voice_capture has a real stream. A browser fixture that forced it open would be measuring markup the product does not paint on a machine with no microphone.

The drill-down slideover, and drill_down is not implemented behind it — no seeded thread in mock.js produces a drill target, so nothing in a browser can open it. Named in this file's header as a gap since it was written; this entry is the same claim in a form the suite can hold to.
The slideover's own backdrop. It cannot be on screen without the slideover above it, so it shares that entry's reason exactly.
The drill-down's chip strip, which is the affordance that OPENS the slideover. Same unreachability and same reason: no seeded conversation carries a drill target.

The rail's scrim on a narrow window — a translucent sheet with no text in it and no boundary of its own, so it is neither a text node nor a non-text INDICATOR under check 3's definition. What matters about a scrim is what can still be read THROUGH it, and check 8 measures exactly that on every run: a 12% sheet takes 4.54:1 down to 4.25:1 and the 4.25 is what gets reported, not the stylesheet's 4.54.

The worker inspector's scrim, on the same footing as the rail's. The inspector ITSELF is walked (surface `inspector`, 146 nodes measured) — it is only the sheet beside it that carries nothing to measure.

floorReference.//: THE ONE RUN EVERY FLOOR BELOW WAS MEASURED IN, and the reason the floors are relative to it. Each `surfaceFloors` entry is a count of the WHOLE PAGE, and every surface but `shell` is the shell plus something — so a change to shared chrome moves all 27 at once. On 2026-09-10 exactly that happened: commit 8397c530 removed the experimental orchestration UI on CEO order, the shell went from 96 of 418 nodes to 92 of 412, and the two floors with the least slack went red about panels that were painting perfectly. Check 9 now subtracts whatever the shell lost in the SAME run before comparing, so shared-chrome drift moves both sides together. Shrink only — a shell that grows raises nobody's floor. Re-derive all of these together, from one run, or not at all: a floor measured against a different shell than this one is the defect this key exists to end.
floorReference.measuredOn: tom-opus-ui1 at 6c02225a, local macOS + Playwright WebKit, two consecutive runs byte-identical on all 27 surfaces
floorReference.toleranceWhy: Three nodes, and the number is bounded from both sides rather than picked. BELOW: the thinnest panel in the set, `first-run-unusable`, contributes 4 measured and 4 considered nodes over the bare shell, so a tolerance of 3 still fails if that panel vanishes — which is the whole job. ABOVE: measured surface-over-shell deltas moved by at most 2 between the 2026-09-06 runner run and this local one, across four days of product change and a different machine, so 3 covers the observed spread with one to spare.

cannotBite.opening-screen: Its floor is 0 of 412 and the bare shell is 92 of 412, so no lower bound on this surface can catch a driver that failed. That is not slack, it is the surface: the opening screen is drawn almost entirely in SVG and contributes exactly ONE HTML text line, which check 9 already reports as unprovable. WHAT PROVES ITS DRIVER ARRIVED INSTEAD: the driver holds the curtain and check 9 prints the curtain's own state with the result — `curtain up and state.reason still null`, read from `RichSplash.state()`. A driver that missed the curtain gets a non-null reason and the check says so by name.
cannotBite.settings: The assertiveness popover ships in index.html and its driver only unhides it, so it adds no text node to the DOM: 412 considered before and after. Its measured count goes DOWN (74 against the shell's 92) because the popover obscures part of the shell, which means the bare shell clears the floor from above rather than falling below it. WHAT PROVES ITS DRIVER ARRIVED INSTEAD: `waitForSelector('#assertiveness-popover:not([hidden])')` followed by `overlaySettled`, both of which throw rather than continuing quietly.
cannotBite.settings-tooltip: The one surface whose whole subject is a string the STYLESHEET renders, in a `::after` pseudo-element — which is not a DOM text node at all, so its counts are the shell's exactly, 92 of 412. A floor over DOM text nodes cannot see the thing this surface exists to measure. WHAT PROVES ITS DRIVER ARRIVED INSTEAD: `pseudoOpaque(p, '.setbtn', '::after')` reads the pseudo-element's own computed opacity and throws if the tooltip never became opaque, and check 11b separately asserts every authored `content` string was measured.

settings-tooltip.//: The shell with the settings button hovered, so the node floor is the shell's own (78/228 — this surface measures 90 of 408 today, exactly as `shell` does). The floor that actually belongs to THIS surface is not a node count: it is check 11b, which requires `style.css`'s `.setbtn::after` content string to be MEASURED in both themes rather than reported hidden, and fails if this driver stops reaching the hover state.
